version.author: TouristKiller
version.changelog: v1.0.5 + Idea Vault: Fixed Swap for tracks scattering the items of an idea with more than one item on a track when the preview audio sat later in the song than where the idea was captured. REAPER keeps a track's items sorted by position, and moving them one by one let an item jump past the others, so some were moved twice and others not at all. The same mistake could misplace items when Load into project fitted a multi-item idea to a slower project tempo. Gluing items before capturing is no longer needed as a workaround. Reported by sridhar

While dragging, the tooltip says which track it will go to. Dropping inside the list still changes the order. version.author: TouristKiller
version.changelog: v1.3.3 + FX node view: Replace FX... in a plugin's right-click menu swaps it for another plugin, picked through the same search and browse menus as Add FX. The new plugin takes over the old one's place: in series or in parallel, the pin routing for the pins both plugins have (so a sidechain stays wired), and a node position you set by hand. It is one undo step, and it is not offered on a container, where it would throw away everything inside. Requested by AndreiMir. + FX node view: Copy FX in the right-click menu, then Paste after this or Replace with copied on another plugin. The copy keeps all its settings and can be pasted on another track too. While something is copied, every Add FX popup (the + and = buttons, and a right-click on the empty canvas) offers it at the top, so it can also go in series, in parallel or at the end of the chain. Requested by AndreiMir.

version.changelog: v0.6.5 + Launcher: Everything that blinks now runs off one clock on the project's beat - the record pads and the record rings included, which kept their own time - and it keeps that beat with the transport stopped. Reported by AndreiMir + Launcher: The Launchpad's own flashing and pulsing is no longer used: a board runs those on its own clock, 120 BPM unless it is fed MIDI clock, so at any other tempo its pads beat against the rest. A playing pad now pulses on the project's beat like everything else + Launcher: The blink follows what the meter counts, an eighth in 6/8 and a quarter in 4/4, the same rule the launch quantize follows + Launcher: A take winding down to its bar line blinks the learned Record pad instead of sitting the same steady red as one that is still running + Launcher: Send to launcher, in the right-click menu of an Items or Source Media card: the route to a clip in another open project tab or a loaded subproject, which nothing that starts from the arrange selection could reach. Asked by AndreiMir + Launcher: An item sent over keeps the trim it was given in its own arrange and brings MIDI that exists only inside that project; a source card comes in as its file, Sync BPM and all + Launcher: The lane is chosen for you - the track the clip came from where this project has one by that name, the selected track otherwise - in the first free row of that lane, and several selected items go over at once + Launcher: A media strip beside the grid - the Items and Source Media lists, narrow - so a clip can be dragged straight into a slot, from this project or from any other open tab. Switch it on under Settings; it is off by default because the grid wants the width. Asked by AndreiMir + Launcher: The strip drag is not an OS drag, both halves being one window, so it works docked as well as floating, and the slot you drop on is the slot it lands in + Launcher: Drag the bar between strip and grid to set its width, and that is remembered; double-click a row instead and the lane is picked for you + Launcher: Hover a strip row for a triangle that auditions it - the clip editor's own preview engine, so it leaves the transport, the edit cursor and every solo alone and can be used mid-jam. Needs SWS; audio only. Asked by AndreiMir + Launcher: With the strip open the project scan keeps running, minus the once-a-second check for missing media, which is the half that costs anything + Launcher: The manual says where the one-project boundary lies now that clips can cross it

version.author: TouristKiller
version.changelog: v1.4.0: + New: Normalize preview, the "norm" button on the transport row. Files from different packs no longer jump in level while you browse. Peak mode brings every file's loudest peak to a target (default -3 dBFS) and works straight away, because it reads the waveform the browser already caches. LUFS mode uses a file's stored LUFS reading and falls back to peak for files that were never analysed, since analysing means putting a temporary track in the project and clicking a file should never do that. The volume knob still works on top of it. Right-click the button for the mode and both targets; the tooltip shows the gain applied to the current file. Requested on the forum + Settings: Show Oscilloscope and Show Waveform checkboxes. The oscilloscope could already be hidden, but only with the small toggle at the end of the transport row, which few people found. With the waveform switched off, the file list takes its space in both layouts. Requested on the forum + Selection: Shift+click now selects a range, the way it does in every other browser, and Ctrl+A selects every file in view. Inserting moved to a double-click or Alt+click; Settings has a switch to turn double-click insert off. A range follows the order on screen, so in Grouped view it skips closed folders and in Tree view it follows the open branches. Tree view supports multi-selection now as well. Requested on the forum + Selection: inserting several files at once. Alt+click on a file that is part of a multi-selection inserts the whole selection end to end on the selected track, starting at the edit cursor and in the order of the list. The right-click menu offers that as well, plus "on separate tracks", which gives each file a new track of its own, named after the file, below the selected one. Both are a single undo step, and the edit cursor ends up after the last inserted file so the next insert follows on. A double-click still inserts just the one file, because its first click has already cleared the selection. Requested on the forum + Selection: the file that was highlighted before a Ctrl- or Shift-click counts as part of the selection, and right-clicking a file outside the selection acts on that file only, rather than on a selection somewhere else in the list + New: a row of your collections above the file list. A collection already works as a free-form label a file can carry any number of, so rather than adding a tag system as a third way of labelling files next to the automatic categories and the collections, the collections themselves are made quicker to use. Click one to show only the files in it, or Ctrl+click to combine several. Right-click one to add the selected files to it or remove them, and + makes a new collection with the selected files in it. Each shows how many files in the list it holds, the collections of the current file are outlined, and the row folds away with its arrow or can be switched off in Settings. A file in Drums / Kick also counts as being in Drums. Requested on the forum + Transport: the minimum display time label ("off" / "1s") and the Auto Key badge are drawn in the same font and colours as auto, sync and tape below them. They used to be in two different styles, one of them hard to read. The oscilloscope toggle now follows the badge instead of landing on top of it, and the left pane can no longer be dragged narrower than the transport needs, so nothing on it gets cut off or overlaps. The transport measures that width itself, because it depends on the fonts and on the key Auto Key shows + Waveform: a selection can be dragged straight from the waveform onto a track, as in REAPER's Media Explorer, and only that section is inserted. Over a selection the cursor turns into a hand: press there and drag. Snapping to the grid, fixed lanes and Shift for a new lane all work as they do when dragging from the file list. A press that does not move still acts as a click (new selection, seek), and dragging outside the selection still makes a new one. The section is not passed to plugin windows or other scripts as a file, because they would receive the whole sample. Until then, a section could only be inserted by dragging the file from the list after selecting part of it. Requested on the forum + Search: typing in the search box no longer lags after every letter. Measured on a 15,000 file location, each letter cost two full filter passes of about 15 ms each: the search bar filtered the list and then the list filtered it again. On top of that, the browser copied the whole visible list on every frame, about 19 ms, whether you were typing or not. Now the text appears in the box at once and the list follows after a short pause in typing, at once on Enter or when you leave the box, and immediately when the box is cleared. The filter runs once and remembers the lower-cased folder names. A letter that only adds to the term searches the previous hits instead of the whole location, which takes under 2 ms. The list copy is only made again when the list itself changes. Tree view was the slowest of all, because it counted the matches per folder by walking the tree: the first search read every folder of the library from disk, and the counting was redone for every visible folder on every frame. Those counts now come from the location's file cache, in one pass per term that takes 5 to 60 ms on the same location, and they match a count taken straight from disk. Reported on the forum + Settings: Settings and Keyboard Shortcuts open in a window of their own, switched with two buttons at the top, instead of taking the place of the file list. Like the browser it has no standard title bar but its own header in the window colour, with the same red close dot, and the sliders have a fixed width so their labels fit without making the window very wide. In a narrow dock the settings page did not fit, so the dock had to be widened every time something needed changing. Now the browser keeps showing its files while you adjust it, so the effect of a setting is visible straight away. The window can float or be docked, and it remembers its size and position. Escape closes it, and while it has focus the arrow keys no longer move through the file list + New: Set Category in the file menu. When the automatic category guesses wrong it can be corrected by hand, for one file or for a whole selection at once, and Automatic puts it back. Corrections are stored per file in CACHE/category_overrides.json and apply everywhere the category is used: the column, sorting and the Auto view

reapack.name: TK_ChordGun.lua
reapack.desc: TK ChordGun - Enhanced chord generator with scale filter/remap and chord recognition

version.author: TouristKiller (based on pandabot ChordGun)
version.changelog:
v2.5.9
[Progression / Timing] + New "Tight Timing" option (Right-Click the PLAY button): progression playback moves out of the defer loop into a JSFX that emits the notes from the audio thread, on the exact sample. The old path picked the start of a chord with roughly 33 ms of slack and then went through StuffMIDIMessage, which waits for the next audio block on top of that - at 120 BPM that is over 6% of a beat, which is what made the progression feel loose against the grid. + Strum and arpeggio no longer stall REAPER. They used to busy-wait on the main thread between notes (five notes at 80 ms froze the UI for 320 ms, which threw the timing of the following chord off as well). They are now onsets the engine schedules against, so they cost nothing and land exactly. + Playback no longer needs a record-armed track: the engine sits at the top of the normal track FX chain instead of the Input FX chain. Notes played this way are heard but not recorded - use INSERT to write the progression into an item. + Starting mid-bar or scrubbing the transport now lands on the chord that belongs at that position instead of restarting the progression. + PLAY shows the playback mode in its colour: blue for Sync Play, green for Tight Timing, teal for both, and orange when Tight Timing is on but the engine is not actually running (no track selected, FX bypassed or missing). + The engine is written into REAPER/Effects on demand and version-locked to the script, so it can never lag behind the data the script writes. With the option off, or no track selected, playback falls back to the previous timing rather than going silent.
[Progression / Chord Length] + New default length for new chords (Right-Click the beats column of the [+] slot panel): 0.5 / 1 / 2 / 4 / 8 beats. Previously every new chord was one beat, so working in bars meant stepping the value up in every single slot by hand. The setting is stored globally, so it survives project and script restarts. Requested by a user who wanted whole-bar or two-bar chords. + Same menu: "Use This Slot's Length As Default" and "Apply Default Length To All Slots". + Chord map templates use the default length as well. Saved presets keep the lengths stored in the file.
[MIDI / Stuck Notes] + Bug fix - notes could be left sounding with no note-off ever following, which a retrospective recording then stretches to the end of the item. stopNotesFromPlaying was driven by the list of the last chord played, so a second chord starting while a first was still sounding orphaned any note that appeared only in the earlier one. It now releases everything that is actually sounding. Reachable through overlapping MIDI triggers and through Hold Mode. Reported by Deodan. + Bug fix - closing the ChordGun window while a chord was sounding left those notes hanging permanently, with no key or button able to rescue them. The window now kills all playing notes on the way out.
[MIDI Trigger] + Bug fix - the "Assign MIDI Trigger" overlay sent you to the top bar to switch the connector icon on. That icon is not in the top bar: it sits in the small column at the right of the chord display, between the dice and the pin. The overlay now says where it actually is. Reported by Deodan.
[Menus] + The Dice right-click menu holds randomize settings only (Progression Length, Always Start on Tonic, Use Selected Chord Types). Playback settings live on PLAY, chord length on the [+] panel. Tooltips now name what a menu contains instead of saying "Settings".
